verdict.rationale: Gate 0 passes structurally. Gate 1: PRD faithfully reflects source analysis and IC. All six ratified IC answers honored without contradiction. All seven IC Open Items addressed (4 resolved in PRD; 3 deferred with explicit forward pointers to design-composer and plan-author). Constraint tension preserved as Constraint A / Constraint B (not pre-decided). Kill-criterion-#1 pause-and-rescope captured in FR-2. Investigation-first cadence captured in FR-1 with the IC's verbatim KB-gap justification. Synthetic-test-feature verification surface captured in FR-6 with real-feature re-run non-gating in FR-7. Affected-files inventory (8 files) matches analysis §6 plus the two schema-bearing artifacts named in the analysis frontmatter. Sweep posture inventory-only per FR-5 with cleanup-as-blocker open-item per AC-FR-5-b. In-flight artifact retrofit explicitly left as-shipped via NFR-6 + Product Policy Decisions table. EARS form is used throughout; minor compound-AC issues are non-blocking. The PRD does NOT silently pre-decide the workaround/specialist-isolation tension. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. Proceed to Gate 2.

issues.location: User Stories § Pipeline Operator, third story
issues.description: User Story 3 says the run terminates 'with a kill-criterion-1-triggered posture and a fresh follow-on feature opened' — implying the follow-on feature creation happens within this run. AC-FR-2-c clarifies that 'the actual creation of the follow-on feature happens outside this run's scope.' The user-story phrasing slightly oversells what this run delivers (a forward pointer, not an opened follow-on feature).
issues.suggestion: Reword the user story to: 'So that I am not exposed to a silent mid-run scope shrink ..., and a forward pointer to a fresh follow-on feature is recorded for later action outside this run.'

issues.location: Functional Requirements § AC-FR-3-a vs. Constraints § 'Constraint tension preserved'
issues.description: The Constraints section states 'the chosen option's rationale (per AC-FR-3-a) must explicitly weigh both constraints' (i.e., both Constraint A workaround-acceptability AND Constraint B specialist-isolation). AC-FR-3-a, however, only requires tying the rationale to '(i) the investigation finding, (ii) the specialist-isolation invariants enumerated in the Constraints section.' Constraint A (workaround acceptability) is not explicitly named in AC-FR-3-a's rationale-tie list. Minor internal gap between the Constraints section's promise and the AC's verifiable requirement.
issues.suggestion: Either (a) extend AC-FR-3-a clause to read '(ii) both Constraint A (workaround acceptability) and Constraint B (specialist-isolation invariants) enumerated in the Constraints section', or (b) reword the Constraints section to say 'the chosen option's rationale must explicitly weigh the specialist-isolation invariants per AC-FR-3-a; the design SHOULD additionally weigh workaround-acceptability when relevant.' Option (a) is preferred for stronger downstream auditability.

issues.description: AC-FR-2-a uses If-then form but chains three distinct actions in one AC ('halt the run', 'emit a kill-criterion-1-triggered posture marker to the checkpoint and state-transitions log', 'produce an analysis artifact under Issues/'). Per EARS Mistake 5 (multiple assertions in one AC), each could pass or fail independently. Non-blocking — the assertions are tightly coupled to the same trigger and a tester would naturally check all three together — but splitting would improve testability.
issues.suggestion: Optionally split into three ACs (AC-FR-2-a halt; AC-FR-2-a' emit-marker; AC-FR-2-a'' produce-analysis-artifact). Lower priority than I-DR-001/002.

issues.location: Functional Requirements § AC-FR-4-a, AC-FR-5-b, AC-FR-6-b, AC-FR-6-c, AC-FR-7-a
issues.description: Five ACs use semicolon to chain two shall-clauses in a single AC (e.g., AC-FR-4-a 'at most eight files; any edit outside surfaced as open item'). EARS-discipline encourages one trigger → one behavior per AC. Each compound AC is mildly less testable; non-blocking.
issues.suggestion: Consider splitting the compound ACs into paired ACs (e.g., AC-FR-4-a edit-budget and AC-FR-4-a' out-of-inventory-edits-as-open-item). Defer to PRD author's judgment; the meaning is clear as-is.

issues.description: FR-7 (real-feature re-run as confidence check) has only one AC (AC-FR-7-a) which captures the recording requirement but does not explicitly state that FR-7's failure does not block feature completion. The non-gating discipline is stated in FR-7's prose body and in the Product Policy Decisions table, but is not encoded as a verifiable AC.
issues.suggestion: Optionally add AC-FR-7-b: 'If the real-feature re-run (FR-7) produces a failed outcome, then the system shall not retroactively invalidate the feature-complete signal issued under FR-6, provided FR-6 passed.' Non-blocking; current wording in prose is acceptable.

issues.location: Prior-run summary claim vs. actual PRD
issues.description: The prior-run / orchestrator summary describes the PRD as having '8 FRs, 7 NFRs, 32 ACs.' Actual AC count is 30 (19 FR ACs + 11 NFR ACs). Discrepancy is in the summary, not the PRD itself, so this is a meta-observation rather than a PRD defect. Recording for traceability.
issues.suggestion: No PRD change needed. The orchestrator's run-summary may be corrected to '30 ACs' for accuracy.
